types: one CLR public type identity maps to one Ruby constant identity
constructors: retain every .ctor identity; dispatch through initialize
overloads: retain every CLR signature identity in the static contract

refOut.refInput: ordinary typed Ruby value input copied at value boundaries
refOut.multipleOut: ordered Array following any non-void CLR return
refOut.singleOutWithReturn: ordered Array of [return value, out value]; the CLR fills its out parameter on every branch, so neither half of the result is dropped

arrayTransforms: caller-owned source/destination Arrays; whole and indexed range forms preserve forward overlap order

collections.genericICollection: preserve the CLR interface identity and project its selected typed members directly on the Ruby collection class
collections.genericIEnumerable: preserve the CLR interface identity; GetEnumerator returns Ruby Enumerator without a fake System namespace
collections.enumerationMutation: fail-fast when the backing collection version changes
collections.indexErrors: a collection index outside 0...Count raises Ruby IndexError, the identity Array#fetch raises, and it is out of range rather than counting from the end; a CopyTo whose destination cannot hold the source raises ArgumentError. CurveKeyCollection established both and every projected collection follows them, so one CLR operation keeps one Ruby behaviour across the binding. This is narrower than the thrownExceptions table's ArgumentOutOfRangeException -> RangeError, which covers a CLR exception a projected member's own IL constructs and rethrows; a collection indexer's out-of-range condition belongs to the backing list, not to the member

staticMembers: class methods; struct-valued members return fresh objects

System.IntPtr.validation: inclusive signed range derived from Fiddle::SIZEOF_VOIDP
System.IntPtr.nativeBoundary: two's-complement bit pattern in the canonical fixed-width C carrier; never Fiddle::Pointer

structs: Ruby classes with boundary copies and dup/clone; assignment aliasing is documented
operators: map to Ruby syntax where available and retain op_* identity in static contract

events.identity: one CLR public event maps to one public Ruby event reader keeping the XNA spelling; never an add_Name/remove_Name pair, never a writer, never a Proc, Array or callback property
events.support: the reader answers the generic CNA::Runtime::Event subscription primitive, whose whole public surface is add/remove
events.subscribe: add(callable) or add { |sender, args| ... } appends one handler and answers the token remove takes back; duplicate subscriptions are permitted
events.unsubscribe: remove(handler) removes the last matching occurrence, as Delegate.Remove does to a multicast invocation list; removing an absent handler is harmless
events.dispatch: registration order, over a snapshot, with exceptions never swallowed
events.raise: internal to the declaring implementation; no consumer-facing emit, fire, trigger or call exists
events.abstract: on an XNA interface contract the event reader raises NotImplementedError like every other member: an interface declares the identity and never owns an invocation list

generics.contract: retain CLR arity/signature and reject ambiguous runtime dispatch
generics.runtimeTypeName: each CLR generic type definition Name`N maps deterministically to NameOfT for arity 1 and NameOfT1T2...TN for higher arity
generics.collisionRule: the non-generic CLR identity keeps Name; no alias may collapse it with the generic identity

expectedMemberFormula: reference public members minus enum value__ metadata storage

bclProjection.register: CNA::Runtime::BclProjection; measured, not aspirational — the API verifier resolves every entry and the dependency frontier consumes the same register
bclProjection.namespace: a projected BCL identity lives in the CNA runtime; no fabricated Ruby ::System namespace is created
bclProjection.scope: only a CLR identity the selected XNA surface actually names, and whose Ruby projection can be decided without guessing, is admitted

exceptions.principle: an XNA exception must behave as a Ruby exception rather than an ordinary Object subclass
exceptions.root: StandardError, because a CLR catch (Exception) is the analogue of a bare Ruby rescue; ::Exception would put XNA failures alongside Ruby's non-recoverable system-level conditions
exceptions.intermediateBases: an intermediate BCL exception class the selected XNA surface never names collapses to the nearest projected ancestor; no Ruby constant is invented for it

thrownExceptions.policy: a CLR exception a projected member throws maps to the nearest Ruby exception with the same meaning, and one CLR exception always maps to exactly one Ruby exception
thrownExceptions.System.ArgumentNullException: ArgumentError; the CLR throws it for a null *or empty* string, so TypeError would be wrong for half its cases
thrownExceptions.System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: RangeError, the same class this binding already raises for a value outside its allowed range

bclProjection.authority: a BCL identity with a real member surface is measured from the pinned Microsoft .NET Framework mscorlib admitted by tools/api_compat/reference/BCL_PROVENANCE.md, never recalled. The measured surface and its derived behavioural facts live in docs/generated/bcl-inventory.json
bclProjection.genericProjection: a projected CLR generic definition answers for every constructed form of itself: ReadOnlyCollection`1[X] resolves to the same Ruby class as ReadOnlyCollection`1. A Ruby class is not statically generic, so the CLR type arguments cannot live in the superclass expression and are carried as class metadata instead, declared with projects_elements and measured by the API verifier under GENERIC_MAPPING_MISMATCH
bclProjection.readOnlyCollection: System.Collections.ObjectModel.ReadOnlyCollection`1 projects to the dedicated support class CNA::Runtime::ReadOnlyCollection, never to Array, a frozen Array, Enumerable alone, Set or an opaque Object. The mscorlib IL settles why: the CLR constructor stores the IList<T> reference and every public read member forwards one call to it, so the wrapper is a live view and a frozen copy would be a different type; the six read members validate nothing of their own; and read-only is a property of the interface, expressed by twelve explicit interface implementations whose whole body throws NotSupportedException unconditionally, which in Ruby is projected as the absence of any mutating member. An XNA class whose CLR base is this generic inherits from the support class, because Ruby has class inheritance and flattening the inherited surface into unrelated methods would lose the CLR base relationship
bclProjection.languageSupport: a support class may carry Ruby-idiomatic identities beside the CLR ones, and they are not XNA identities. CNA::Runtime::ReadOnlyCollection declares each, the single Ruby identity that carries CLR GetEnumerator, and includes Enumerable, every method of which Ruby derives from each alone. The two sets are separable by construction: a CLR identity is PascalCase or an operator, language support is not

constructorFreeClasses: a CLR class whose only constructor is internal projects to a Ruby class with `new` made private, as GraphicsResource and Texture already do; its public non-constructibility is part of the contract and the internal construction path stays reachable to a future producer through __send__. No producer is fabricated, and no public Ruby constructor is created that XNA does not expose.
